hooks.text: Built for twenty-one months, it flew for over thirty years.
Could a fragile probe survive the asteroid belt and reach Jupiter?
Pioneer ten carried a cosmic roadmap and nude drawings into deep space.

title: The 21-Month Spacecraft That Flew for Thirty Years
description: Pioneer 10 braved the asteroid belt and Jupiter to carry humanity's golden message across the stars.

beats.text: Built for twenty-one months, it flew for over thirty years.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of Pioneer 10 in deep space, NASA, 1972

beats.text: Most people assumed deep space hazards would kill the probe, but Pioneer ten defied expectations.
beats.visual: Pioneer 10 model in cleanroom assembly at TRW, 1971

beats.text: In March nineteen seventy-two, an Atlas-Centaur rocket launched the historic craft from Earth.
beats.visual: Atlas-Centaur carrying Pioneer 10 liftoff from Cape Canaveral, 1972
queries: Atlas Centaur Pioneer F launch Cape Canaveral

beats.text: The spacecraft became the first to safely navigate through the treacherous asteroid belt.
beats.visual: Artist concept of Pioneer 10 passing through the asteroid belt, NASA, 1972

beats.text: It survived brutal Jovian radiation to capture stunning close-up views of the Great Red Spot.
beats.visual: Pioneer 10 close-up photograph of Jupiter and the Great Red Spot, 1973

beats.text: Bolted to its antenna strut was a gold-anodized plaque designed by Carl Sagan and Frank Drake.
beats.visual: The Pioneer Plaque showing the human figures and pulsar map, NASA, 1972

beats.text: The message carried drawings of nude humans and a map pointing back to Earth.
beats.visual: Pioneer plaque high resolution detail of human figures, NASA, 1972

beats.text: Today, this silent ghost ship carrying our map drifts toward the constellation Taurus, defying its original design.
beats.visual: The star Aldebaran in the constellation Taurus, astrophotography, 2020
